overview: This three-letter file documents efforts in February 1935 to arrange a U.S. State Department interview for Mrs. William M. Hosken of the Hosken Trading Company concerning a proposed large-scale pharmaceutical trade venture with Hajime Hoshi of the Hoshi Pharmaceutical Company. Japanese Consul General Renzo Sawada introduces Hosken to Eugene H. Dooman of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Dooman promises appropriate assistance, and Hosken Trading Company subsequently supplies her Washington itinerary. Although catalogued under Formosa/Taiwan manufactures, drugs, toilet articles, and perfumes—and cross-filed under quinine—the correspondence itself focuses on American-Japanese pharmaceutical commerce and informal official facilitation.

subfiles.title: Hosken Trading Company letter arranging Mrs. Hosken's interview
subfiles.from: Hosken Trading Co., Inc., signed by its secretary (OCR: “a hadskin”)
subfiles.to: Eugene Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: The company advises Dooman of Mrs. Hosken's arrival in Washington and asks him to choose a convenient time to meet her.
subfiles.summary: Hosken Trading Company reports that Renzo Sawada said Dooman would be willing to receive Mrs. W. M. Hosken. It states that she will arrive at the Shoreham Hotel on February 28 and will keep the following Friday free for an appointment. State Department receipt and filing stamps show that the letter was processed in early March 1935.

subfiles.title: Sawada introduction of Mrs. Hosken and pharmaceutical trade proposal
subfiles.from: Renzo Sawada, Consulate General of Japan, New York
subfiles.to: Eugene Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Sawada introduces Mrs. Hosken and describes her proposed pharmaceutical trade cooperation with Hajime Hoshi.
subfiles.summary: Sawada explains that Mrs. William M. Hosken and Hajime Hoshi have been negotiating a large-scale plan to promote American-Japanese trade in pharmaceutical products. Hosken wants the views of official circles in Washington, while Sawada offers to serve as an intermediary on the Japanese side if the proposal develops. He asks Dooman to interview her and, if possible, introduce her to another official interested in pharmaceutical commerce. Filing notations cross-reference the correspondence to quinine and another decimal-file number.

subfiles.title: Dooman reply promising assistance to Mrs. Hosken
subfiles.to: Renzo Sawada, Consul General of Japan
subfiles.about: Dooman acknowledges Sawada's introduction and agrees to assist Mrs. Hosken if she calls on him.
subfiles.summary: Dooman acknowledges Sawada's February 22 letter introducing Mrs. William M. Hosken of the Hosken Trading Company. He assures Sawada that he will be pleased to give her all appropriate assistance should she visit him. The surviving page identifies itself as a true copy of the signed original.

interest: The file offers a compact example of commercial diplomacy operating through personal introductions rather than formal negotiations: a Japanese consul connected a private American merchant with a State Department specialist on Japan. The three documents preserve the full administrative sequence—introduction, official acceptance, and appointment logistics—and show how a proposed private pharmaceutical venture sought governmental opinion and support. The quinine cross-reference is also useful for reconstructing how State Department clerks classified overlapping trade, drug, and regional subjects, while the mismatch between the broad Formosa/Taiwan file title and the letters' actual content illustrates the quirks of the decimal filing system.
